why: The kept slice sl-intent-to-design holds the same four features as the shaped slice, in the same order: fn-795, fn-818, fn-798 and fn-898. Each of them serves business intent bi-788. So no feature is pulled in and no feature is pushed out. The shaped slice differs from the kept slice only in its name, which the product owner changed (change-round2.md item 1); a new name changes no feature. The slice keeps its one surface (the Claude Code command line), its tester (the product owner) and its four features, so it stays testable end to end. No slice is in progress, so the kept slice may be used.

decisions.question: Which slice serves this business intent, and does it change?
decisions.answer: The kept slice sl-intent-to-design serves bi-788. Its features do not change: pull in none, push out none, because its features are the shaped slice's features and each serves bi-788. Only its name changes, by the product owner's change.
